## Target
`src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — **791 LOC** on origin/main @ 059d54b725, against the 800-LOC hard
cap. Nine lines of headroom, inside the gate's `>= 720` near-cap warning band.

## Why this is filed late
It was excluded from this epic's original scope on 2026-08-19 because in-flight work owned the file
(`masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle`, the P1 root-disk RCA). That ticket has since CLOSED, so nothing
claims the file today and it is the only near-cap file in the band with no owner. Re-measure before
planning: main moved substantially during this epic.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH. `_config_sources.py` sits below the config
seam that RP-04 spent several stories establishing, so respect that boundary — this is a split
along an existing concern, not a re-architecture of config ownership.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically. NAME the boundary in
  the commit message and say why the call graph supports it.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 each. Leave REAL headroom.
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area pass UNMODIFIED.

## Lessons from the five splits that landed before this one — apply all of them
1. **Check both sides of the binding.** What monkeypatches the symbols you MOVE, and what
   monkeypatches the symbols your moved code CALLS. The `config.py` split (Gerrit 1932) caused a
   real behaviour change this way: a test patched `config.repo_root`, the moved function rebound it
   from its new sibling at import time, and the code wrote outside the tmp root. Resolve such names
   through the composition root at call time.
2. **Update path-keyed registries in the same change.** Allowlists, line budgets, ownership
   registries, golden files, census tests and `<file>:<line>` doc citations. Several live INSIDE
   test files. `docs/env-vars.md` is CI drift-gated and records `<file>:<line>` for non-literal
   `os.environ.get` reads — a config-adjacent split is very likely to shift those; regenerate.
3. **Two complexity-baseline traps.** The baseline is keyed `<path>::<symbol>`. MOVING a baselined
   symbol adds a key (`new>0`, CI fails). REDUCING complexity inside one makes it stale — which
   PASSES `make lint` and FAILS CI. Run `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
   directly and require `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`. Never edit the baseline file.
4. **Validate against the whole tree.** CI runs everything; two agents were caught by failures in
   `tests/interfaces` after validating only `tests/unit`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` is under the cap with REAL headroom, and every new file is
      >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED, including any test
      that monkeypatches a symbol this module defines OR calls.
- [ ] The public import surface is unchanged: no symbol previously resolvable through
      `rebar._config_sources` stops resolving. Proven by comparing `dir()` against pre-split main.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`,
      and `.github/module-size-limit.txt` and `.github/complexity-baseline.json` are unmodified.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, and any CI drift-gated generated artifact
      (e.g. `docs/env-vars.md`) is regenerated in the same change.
